basis.note: growth scaled to one game-year; archive shorter than 0.5 game-years: earliest pull used; span under 0.1 game-years: growth not measured

definitions.players: every player aged 16-26 at the latest pull; age = the pull's Age field (age on the pull's in-game date; the DEV grid uses Jan-1 ages)
definitions.role: P when pos is SP, RP or CL, else H
definitions.grow: sum over the core skills (H BABIP GAP POW EYE K; P STU HRR PBABIP CON) of (display at to - display at from) / 5, display = mean of vR and vL, divided by the span in game-years, rounded to 0.5; null without an earlier pull, and null when he was out of an org at the earlier pull (lev AMA, FA, INT or blank: his card there may be hidden; note 'out of an org a year ago: growth unknown')
definitions.pot_delta: OOTP Pot grade at to minus at from, over the span, not scaled; pot_dir = up / flat / down; null on the same out-of-an-org rule as grow
definitions.core_sum: sum over the core skills of underlying(display) on the dev_odds internal scale
definitions.odds: dev_odds grid cell role / age / Pot bucket / growth bucket (odds_cell); the grid has a cell for every age 16-26; null when the cell has n < 15 (note says so); a player without growth uses the pot_only cell (odds_cell ends in /any)
definitions.vs_typical: core_sum minus the MEDIAN core_sum of this league's own players of the same age and Pot bucket (peer group >= 20), internal points; the DEV mean is the fallback for a thin peer group (vs_typical_basis says which)
definitions.flag: keep = grow >= 4.5 (H) or >= 3 (P) and pot_dir not down; move = pot_dir down and grow <= 2 (H) or <= 1 (P); else null
definitions.level: Lev from the app's hitters.json / pitchers.json, else the archive's lev, else null
definitions.peak: peak_p25 / peak_p50 / peak_p75 = the eventual peak WAA (p25, p50, p75) of the DEV players in the same cell (peak_cell, same key as odds_cell; dev_odds 'peak', or 'peak_pot_only' when growth is unknown, cell ends in /any); DEV peak = max engine now_WAA over the player's later dumps, players seen at age >= 27 only; a growth cell with n < 15 falls back to the pot-only cell of the same age and Pot (note: 'thin growth cell'), and only when that is thin too are the peak fields null (note says thin); peak_n = the cell's n
definitions.share_now: the player's current WAA the conditional fields start from: hitters 'Max WAA wtd', pitchers the larger of 'WAA wtd' and 'WAA wtd RP' from the app's hitters.json / pitchers.json, the same now the DEV cache priced its own players on (agecurve_fit.py) and the org builder's currentValue; null when he is in neither file
definitions.share_basis: which lookalikes the conditional fields read: 'now tercile' = the dev_odds by_now sub-cell of his cell whose now range holds share_now, used when it has n >= 15, gain-distance rule; 'now tercile, edge' = share_now sits above the top sub-cell's hi or below the bottom sub-cell's lo (outside every lookalike's current; a now in the small gap between two sub-cells is not an edge), so the chance is the LOWER of the gain rule and the nearest sub-cell's own peak-level share (its mlb / useful / good): the gain rule alone would lend a player above the group gains measured on players who were never where he is, and the sub-cell share alone would credit a player below the group with better players' outcomes; 'whole cell' = the cell's gain_grid when the nearest sub-cell is thin, gain rule; prefix 'pot-only, ' when the pot-only cell stood in; null when share_now is null (then peak_mlb / peak_useful / peak_good are the cell shares as is)
definitions.listed_peak: the app's listed peak: MAX WAA P (hitters) or the larger of WAP and WAP RP (pitchers) from public/data/<LG>/hitters.json and pitchers.json; null when the player is in neither file
definitions.peak_vs_listed: peak_p50 minus listed_peak, one decimal; null when either is null
definitions.peak_gain: peak_gain_p25 / peak_gain_p50 / peak_gain_p75 = the gain of his lookalikes (p25, p50, p75): each DEV player's eventual peak WAA minus his now-WAA at that dump; never below 0; from the now-tercile sub-cell's gain_grid when share_basis is a tercile (so the gain is conditional on his current: a player near the top of his cell gets the smaller gain of the lookalikes who were already there), else the whole cell's dev_odds gain_p25 / gain_p50 / gain_p75; null when the cell has n < 15, the same rule as peak_p50; the app's growth target (Proj Potential) is the player's current WAA + peak_gain_p50
definitions.peak_mlb: the chance his eventual peak reaches -1 WAA (an MLB-level player, a 5th starter or bench bat) FROM WHERE HE IS NOW: the share of his lookalikes' gains at or above (-1 - share_now), read off the gain grid share_basis names, linear between the grid's quantile levels (5, 10, ..., 95): 1.0 when the distance is <= 0.05 (at the bar, or under it by no more than the app's one-decimal display rounding: a row shown as 0.0 can sit at -0.02 and must not read under 100%), 1.0 down to 0.95 below the 5% quantile, 0.05 down to 0 between the 95% quantile and twice it; a player already at or above the bar reads 1.0 (user, 2026-09-24: 'there are a ton of guys who are already at 0+ WAA that are getting like tagged as less than 100% to reach it', and 'guys already at 0+ WAA tagged as less than 100% is obviously not intended'); when share_basis is an edge the chance is the lower of the gain rule and the nearest sub-cell's own share whose eventual peak reached the bar, still 1.0 at the bar; the org builder orders minors playing time by this chance first (user, 2026-09-24: 'if they will ever be anything in the mlb'); null when the cell has n < 15, the same rule as peak_p50
definitions.peak_useful: peak_useful / peak_good = the same conditional chance at 0 WAA (an average MLB player) and +1.5 (a star), bars from dev_odds peak_bars; user, 2026-09-24: Make it % is playing time, not quality, these say whether the lookalikes turned out good enough
definitions.cell_shares: cell_mlb / cell_useful / cell_good = the cell's own mlb_share / useful_share / good_share (the share of the whole cell whose eventual peak reached each bar, blind to his current), for reference; the app reads peak_mlb / peak_useful / peak_good
